newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end weak but HK Telecom makes firm gains.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end weak but HK Telecom makes firm gains.

text.p: Hong Kong blue chips ended weak on Wednesday as interest rate concerns continued to dampen sentiment in the market but utility stocks moved higher, led by firm gains in Hongkong Telecom shares. The Hang Seng Index fell 39.32 points, or 0.29 percent, to 13,410.76. Turnover was a busy HK$10.73 billion compared with HK$10.26 billion on Tuesday.
"The real story today is Hongkong Telecom," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sale trader at NAVA SC Securities.
Talk that Cable & Wireless Plc would sell part of its Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd stake to a Chinese party drove shares in Hongkong Telecom HK$0.40 higher to HK$14.15.
"It is just a resurfacing of all those stories," said Galbraith.
A spokesman for Hongkong Telecom declined to comment.

"I guess there is a high chance of this happening because I think the Chinese government will want to have a stake in the telecom business in Hong Kong," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
"This stock has been a laggard for some time," he added.
Chia said investors were also bidding up shares of smaller cap companies in the hope that Chinese companies would be seeking backdoor listings by buying stakes.
He pointed to Shun Shing Holdings which gained HK$0.85 to HK$3.225 on Wednesday.
Since Shun Shing announced last week that COSCO (H.K.) Property Development had raised its stake in the company to 61 percent from 30 percent, the stock has jumped 226 percent.
Chia said Sui Chong and Fung Cheung Kee were benefiting from the speculation. Sui Chong rose HK$0.29 to HK$0.80 and Fung Cheung rose HK$0.125 to HK$0.37.

Analysts said the rest of the market was quiet as investors awaited the second phase of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony later and U.S. employment data due on Friday.
"I think the major concern now is the rising U.S. long bond yield," said Chia. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 14/32 on Tuesday to yield 6.87 percent.
Shares in HSBC Holdings rebounded to end HK$1.50 higher at HK$188.00 but Hang Seng Bank remained under pressure falling HK$1.25 to HK$83.50.
